problem: For integers r>=2, k>=1, a_1..a_k>=1, b>=1 let P(q) = [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q * [b]_{q^r}, where [n]_q = 1+q+...+q^{n-1} and [b]_{q^r} = 1+q^r+...+q^{r(b-1)}. P is (weakly) unimodal if its coefficients satisfy c_0<=...<=c_m>=...>=c_N for some m. U = {b : P unimodal}, F = sum floor(a_i/r), D = sum(a_i-1). Question: exactly which parameters make P unimodal? (Source: arXiv:2605.12822, Conjecture 5.4.)

claims.description: Counterexample to condition O_rho of the residue certificate (R2E2 Theorem R). Instance: r=57, residue parts rho = (1 repeated 37 times, 6,7,9,15,18,20,22,23,25,26,27,28,30,33,37), k=52, sigma = sum(rho_i - 1) = 311. P_2(rho) = prod[rho_i]_q [2]_{q^57} is not unimodal, so N*(rho)=1 and the explorer reports K_1=141 (K as defined in R2E2 Theorem R). mu*_inf = max{u: f_u < tau_u} with f = coefficients of 1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)) and tau = residue-class sums (period r, extended periodically to all integers u) of (1-q)prod[rho_i]_q, equals -16; with 36 ones (k=51) mu*_inf=14. Hence 2mu*_inf+3r = 139 <= 141 and O fails at j=1 for k=52. Also: lifts of this instance satisfy S2 (U=[1,40]u{42} etc.).
claims.statement: Let r=57 and rho = (1^37, 6,7,9,15,18,20,22,23,25,26,27,28,30,33,37) (k=52 parts). Claims: (1) prod_i [rho_i]_q * [2]_{q^57} is NOT weakly unimodal, while prod_i [rho_i]_q * [1]_{q^57} is. (2) With tau_u = sum of coefficients of q^e in (1-q)prod_i[rho_i]_q over e == u (mod 57) (so tau is 57-periodic in u) and f_u = coefficient of q^u in 1/((1-q)^{51}(1-q^57)) for u>=0 (f_u=0 for u<0), the largest integer u (over all integers, u>=-57) with f_u < tau_u is u=-16 (mu*_inf=-16). (3) With 36 ones instead of 37 (k=51, f from 1/((1-q)^{50}(1-q^57))), that largest u is 14.
claims.numbers: P_1 unimodal, P_2 not; mu*_inf=-16 (k=52); mu*_inf=14 (k=51).

claims.description: Four-middle rule (R3E6 rule_gen). DOMAIN: r>=4; r divides no a_i; exactly four a_i have residue a_i mod r in [2,r-2]; every other a_i has residue 1 or r-1. DEFINITIONS: drop parts equal to 1; k' = number of remaining parts (parts >= 2). D = sum_i (a_i-1). tau in Z^r: tau_t = sum of the coefficients of q^e in (1-q)*prod_i [a_i mod r]_q over all e == t (mod r) ([n]_q = 1+q+...+q^{n-1}). mu = max{j in [1,r-1]: tau_j>0} (0 if none). T6 = 1+floor((D+1-2mu)/r). f_i = coefficient of q^i in 1/((1-q)^(k'-1)(1-q^r)) = sum_{m>=0, rm<=i} C(i-rm+k'-2, k'-2) for i>=0, and f_i = 0 for i<0. RULE: P_b = prod_i [a_i]_q [b]_{q^r} is unimodal iff b <= T6-2, or b in {T6-1, T6} and LOW(b) holds, where for K = D+1-r(b+1) and m0 = max(1, -floor((K-1)/2)), LOW(b) means: (a) f_{K+m} + tau_{(-m) mod r} >= 0 for every integer m in [m0, min(r*b, m0+r)], and (b) K < 1 or 1 - f_K <= tau_0. For b > T6 P_b is not unimodal. Fit: exhaustive r=4..10, four middle parts < 3r and 0..3 extra parts of residue 1 or r-1 below 3r: 1,213,632 instances, 0 errors; random r<=120, k<=19, a_i<=400 (about 9,300 instances), 0 errors.

CLAIMED NUMBERS: exhaustive over r=4..10 with four middle parts each < 3r (as a multiset) plus 0..3 extra parts of residue 1 or r-1, each < 3r: 1,213,632 instances, 0 errors (and in all of them U is [1,T6] or [1,T6-2]).

claims.description: Stabilization rule (R3E7 rule_stab). DOMAIN/DEFINITIONS: r divides no a_i, all a_i>=2. s_i = a_i mod r, k = number of parts, S = sum s_i, K0 = S-k+1, F = sum floor(a_i/r). tau_t = sum over e == t (mod r) of the coefficients of q^e in (1-q)prod_i [s_i]_q. w_n = coefficient of q^n in 1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)) (0 for n<0). For e>=1 let Delta_e = K0 - r(e+1) and W(Delta) = {integers m: Delta/2 < m <= Delta/2 + r}. mu = max{t in [0,r-1]: tau_t>0}, T = 1+floor((K0-2mu)/r). U_inf = {1} u {e in [2,T]: w_m - w_{Delta_e - m} >= tau_{m mod r} for all m in W(Delta_e)}. For a multiset Z of positive integers let h^Z = coefficients of prod_{z in Z}(1-q^z) / ((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)); H(Z) holds iff h^Z_m - h^Z_{Delta_e-m} >= tau_{m mod r} for every e in U_inf with e>=2 and every m in W(Delta_e). Z(a) = multiset of the parts a_i < r. RULE (on the domain where H(Z(a)) holds): P_b = prod[a_i]_q [b]_{q^r} is unimodal iff b <= F+1 or b-F in U_inf. CONJECTURE Q: an instance is 'stable' (U = [1,F] u (F+U_inf)) iff H(Z(a)) holds. Fit: 8,000 random instances r<=60, k<=140, a_i<=400; 60,193 (a,b) pairs 0 errors; sharp L0* = L0_hyb = least t>=2 with H({s_i: s_i >= t}) on 31,779 exhaustive residue multisets r in [3,8], k in [2,10].

claims.description: Near-miss in the search for a global S2 counterexample at large r (R3E4). Instance r=8000, a=(12871,12875,12921,20863,20986), F=7. Exact brute force: P_b unimodal for b=6,7,8 and not for b=9..13; i.e. U intersect [6,13] = {6,7,8}. Also N*=beta=8 in the class-pair criterion. In 316,601 float-engine evaluations with r in [1000,50000] no S2 failure (beta-N* always 0 or 2).
claims.statement: Let r=8000, a=(12871,12875,12921,20863,20986), P_b = prod_i [a_i]_q [b]_{q^r}. Claim: for b in {6,...,13}, P_b is weakly unimodal exactly for b in {6,7,8}. Also P_b is weakly unimodal for every b in {1,...,5}.
